# SYNTHESIS — SILENT-PASS is a property of an edge, not of a function

**Status: a hypothesis generated by two failed runs and one adversarial
adjudication. It licenses a preregistration. It licenses nothing else, and
nothing in this document should be cited as a result.**

---

## the two failures

Both instruments built on 2026-08-21 were measured against criteria frozen before
they were written. Both fell short, and **they fell short in opposite directions**.

**`styxx.contract`** (`RESULT_contract_sp6_2026_08_21.md`) inspects the **call
boundary**: was there anything to measure, and did it claim something anyway?
Replayed against real pre-fix source for the 5 SP-6 cases:

- boundary-degenerate — nothing arrives, something confident leaves — **3 of 3**
- interior-degenerate — a *well-formed* argument arrives and the emptiness is
  manufactured inside — **0 of 2, unreachable at any tuning**

Kill criterion was ≥ 4 of 5. It scored 3. Dead as stated.

**`styxx.flattering`** (`RESULT_flattering_external_2026_08_21.md`) inspects the
**returned value**: is this constant the reassuring end of its scale? Across
19,632 files of third-party Python:

- 8 candidates, **0 genuine**, 24 of 24 refuted unanimously
- recall on its own training corpus: **2 of 20 — 10%**

## the shape they share

`contract` looks at one endpoint. `flattering` looks at the other. Neither
works, and the adversarial adjudication — written by reviewers whose assigned job
was to *refute* my findings, not to help me — named the reason without being
asked to:

> **C1 — no consumer-liveness analysis. Kills 6 of 6.**
> *"Does the symbol have any reader outside its writing scope?"*
> `_validated` has zero external readers. Both numpy call sites discard the
> return. scipy's `stop_criteria` declares the parameter and never dereferences it.

> **C6 — the defect class definitionally requires an outbound measurement a
> downstream reader misinterprets; a value travelling inward is categorically
> ineligible.**

C6 is a definition, and it is not one I wrote. Read it as a claim about where the
defect lives:

> **A value is not "flattering". A value is flattering *to someone*.**
> `0.0` is a defect only where a consumer thresholds it. `True` is a defect only
> where a consumer branches on it. With no consumer, `risk = 0.0` computed from
> nothing is not a silent pass — it is a number nobody read.

This is why `flattering`'s vocabulary filter inverted on it. `valid`, `assert`,
`check` are the words libraries use for **one-sided predicates**, where an
optimistic empty return is *mathematically correct* — vacuous truth, arity zero,
the supremum of an empty set. The filter selected for the construct where the
pattern is benign and deselected for the construct where it is dangerous. Name
polarity is a property of one node. The defect is not.

## the claim

> **SILENT-PASS is a property of an edge in the dataflow graph: an edge from a
> producer whose value may be unmeasured, to a consumer that makes a decision on
> it, across which no validity information travels.**
>
> Neither endpoint is the defect. The producer is entitled to return `0.0`. The
> consumer is entitled to threshold. The failure is that the edge carries a
> number and drops the answer to *"is this a number at all?"*

Three prior results are the same statement in other vocabulary, which is the
main reason to take it seriously:

- **`styxx.loops`** found that a contaminated field corrupts consumers through
  the **join** — the defect was never in `outcome`, it was in the six places that
  trusted it. One field, six consumers, findable only by asking *where does this
  come from and who trusts it?*
- **`_entropy_topk`** (found today): the guard
  `sum(Hs)/len(Hs) if Hs else float("nan")` is **correct and always was**. An
  honest refusal upstream, defeated by a flattering default one level down. Both
  endpoints defensible; the edge between them is where it broke.
- **`diffgate.only_touches`** (found today): `outside` is empty, so
  `"VERIFIED" if not outside` is *vacuously true*. The producer (`parse_unified_diff`
  returning `{}`) and the consumer (a scope check) are each individually
  reasonable. Neither knows the diff failed to parse.

## what this reframes

`Measured` stops being a utility type and becomes the thesis.

It does not judge the value. It makes the value **refuse to cross the edge
silently**: `.value` raises, `bool()` raises, comparison raises. A consumer that
thresholds an unmeasured value gets an exception rather than a reading. That is
not a convenience wrapper — it is edge enforcement at the type level, and it is
why it works where two static screens did not.

It also explains the ceiling every previous instrument hit. `absence` (0/5 on
SP-6), `absence`+`loops` (1/5), `contract` (3/5, boundary only), `flattering`
(10% recall) are all **node analyses aimed at an edge property**. Their ceilings
are not tuning failures. They are the wrong shape.

## the one thing that would falsify it

If an edge-aware screen — producer of a possibly-unmeasured value → consumer that
branches or thresholds on it, with no validity channel between — does **not**
outperform both node screens on a corpus neither was built from, the reframe is
wrong and node analysis was simply underpowered.

An exploratory probe (`scripts/consumer_probe.py`, explicitly not a test)
suggests the ranking signal exists: the highest-consequence functions in the
TIER-B pool are consumed by many decisions — `str_to_bool` (27), 
`is_torch_xla_available` (26), `allEqual` (17) — and **name polarity does not find
any of them.** Decision-count and name vocabulary are different orderings.

## conditions on the next run, fixed now

Written here so they cannot be softened after seeing an output:

1. **A positive control declared in advance.** The external flattering run had
   none, and `0 of 8` was uninterpretable the moment it printed — a screen with
   zero recall and a defect-free corpus produce byte-identical output. That is
   this project's own defect class, committed by this project's own experiment,
   and it must not happen twice.
2. **A corpus of evaluation, monitoring, gating and safety code** — not numerics.
   Scanning 19,632 files of `site-packages` was scanning the wrong organ.
3. **Precision AND recall both preregistered**, with the two-sided rule: if
   precision is high because the screen barely fires, that goes in the title.
4. **Adjudication by reviewers prompted to refute**, as here. It is the only
   reason today's numbers are trustworthy — three of the eight refutations
   depended on facts I had not checked, and one of them corrected a specific
   *I had fabricated* in the claim itself.

## the honest summary

Two instruments were built, measured against criteria frozen in advance, and both
failed. The failures were not noise: they were **complementary**, and their
complement has a name. Every previous instrument in this program has been a node
analysis aimed at an edge property, which is why they all hit a ceiling and why
the ceiling moved when `Measured` — the only edge-level construct built so far —
was introduced.

That is worth one preregistration. It is not worth a claim.
